items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Edgar Hayes was the greatest I had ever heard and I was working with him and hearing him every night.

ctx.x: That summer I went to Centerville for a vacation and stayed with Uncle John who had 3 daughters, Matty, Ida and Cora, A son named John Albert Coleman after his father. Matty and Ida were older than John and I. Ida played the Piano and was the organist at the Baptist church. For playing hymns, Ida was alright but when she played sheet music (popular songs) she would not give the measures their proper value. She could read very well but in some places, she just didn't have rhythm. Nevertheless, we used to have some…

Before coming back to Cincinnati, I stayed a couple of days in Paris and there was a dance one night with an orchestra called Edgar Hayes and his Collegians. I learned that the musicians were going to Wilberforce University and Edgar Hayes had

persuaded them to spend their summer vacation in Lexington, Ky., his home town, and play the summer dance season in Kentucky. The original leader of the band was Horace Henderson, a pianist, but he was not with the band then, because Edgar Hayes was also a pianist and a hell of a good one. Some of the musicians in the band at that time were Joe and Casper McCord and Henry Hicks.
